newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium premium spikes by LME end, focus nearby.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium premium spikes by LME end, focus nearby.

text.p: Aluminium nearby backwardations were the focus of attention during Monday afternoon LME trading, with increased cash/Sept tightness helping to stave off falls in forward prices.
Traders said once an active pricing against the August "third Wednesday" passed by, the attention in aluminium switched towards borrowing and rolling forward of cash prompts.
The spread in demand was cash/September, which traded out from $41 backwardation to $65 as shorts opted to roll forward in order to secure metal or warrants over the next month to deliver.
Comparatively less interest was seen in the three months market, which, although lower, proved to be resilient on the downside.

Prices bottomed out at $1,656 a tonne before closing at $1,677, still down $24 from Friday's kerb close. The cash/threes backwardation widened out to $55/60, due to the cash/Sept borrowing. On Friday, the benchmark spread was around $31.
Elsewhere in the complex a generally lower tone prevailed, which reflected the fresh losses in copper. The midsession pricing was lively, without any significant surprises, they added.
Copper was again hit by liquidation, following on from last Friday, with prices dropping to near seven-month lows of $2,153 at one stage.
Another rise in stocks, as well as the market being in a $4/6 cash/threes contango, underlined current negative sentiment. Last kerb trade was at $2,162, down $51.
Zinc prices fell under the $1,500 level during the afternoon sessions, briefly uncovering some sell-stops down to a low of $1,480 before last trade at $1,492, down $32.

Traders said the trend reflected patterns elsewhere, notably a response to the pressured copper market. However, the pace of trading was slow, with the fall under $1,500 more of a mark-down rather than a sell-off.
In the short-term, September tightness is likely to maintain caution on the downside, they said.
Nickel prices fluctuated in a fairly wide band throughout, but were steadier for most of the session - a trend that reflected a heavily oversold market. Last business was at $6,670, up $40.
Meanwhile, at the Falconbridge Sudbury dispute the union said Monday it expects an agreement with the company soon on shift scheduling.
Tin was mostly quiet, closing at $5,370, down $10. Lead was generally routine as well, holding above $600, but still finishing $5 lower at $610. Alloy ended at a slightly lower $1,500/10.
